macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global stocks rise ahead of central-bank decisions and major earnings
items.summary: Global equities and bonds advanced as investors prepared for a week of central-bank meetings and results from major technology companies. U.S. stocks opened higher, with the Dow up 0.52%, the S&P 500 up 0.96%, and the Nasdaq up 1.23%; oil prices eased from six-month highs.[1]

items.title: Markets expect Fed to hold rates, but December hike odds rise
items.summary: Investors broadly expect the Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting, while market pricing implies roughly an 80% chance of a December hike as inflation remains elevated. The ECB and Bank of Japan are also expected to hold rates, while New Zealand’s central bank is widely expected to raise rates.[1][4]

items.title: Wall Street focuses on inflation, GDP and central-bank risk
items.summary: This week’s U.S. data include consumer confidence, third-quarter GDP and the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge. September PCE inflation is expected to remain well above the Fed’s 2% target, increasing concern that rates could stay higher for longer.[6][8]

items.title: Mega-cap technology earnings dominate the week
items.summary: Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon are scheduled to report quarterly results, alongside Intel and Sandisk. The reports are expected to provide a major test of investor confidence in artificial-intelligence spending and the broader technology rally.[2][5]

items.title: Asian markets open cautiously as oil retreats
items.summary: Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.5% and South Korea’s benchmark dropped 1.1%, while European equity futures rose and U.S. futures edged higher. Brent crude pulled back from a six-month peak amid continued concern over Middle East supply disruptions.[2][5]

items.title: SpaceX debt financing pressures some AI infrastructure stocks
items.summary: Neocloud companies declined after Elon Musk said SpaceX had completed a $40 billion debt raise connected to a transaction involving Apollo Global Management and the leasing of data-center hardware and AI chips.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $80,000 after weekend sell-off
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered to about $80,720 after falling to roughly $79,146 over the weekend, while more than $810 million in crypto positions were liquidated. The move followed Bitcoin’s first close below its 50-day moving average since August.

items.title: CoinDCX reports $15.99 million loss from retired wallets
items.summary: Indian crypto exchange CoinDCX said approximately $15.99 million in USDT was lost from operational wallets retired after a July 2025 breach, citing a failure in its deposit-sweeping service.

items.title: Malaysia and Thailand join Singapore-led stablecoin settlement project
items.summary: The central banks of Malaysia and Thailand joined Singapore’s BLOOM initiative, which explores cross-border payments using regulated stablecoins and tokenized bank deposits.

items.title: OCC finalizes U.S. stablecoin rules for January 2027
items.summary: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued final rules under the GENIUS Act, including a two-business-day ordinary redemption-processing limit and notification requirements for unusually large redemption volumes.

items.title: Quant token jumps as tokenized-deposit initiative gains attention
items.summary: Quant rose about 18% in 24 hours to approximately $217 and more than doubled over 30 days. The rally followed The Clearing House’s selection of Quant to support an initiative for clearing tokenized bank deposits.

items.title: Ireland fines Coinbase €3.25 million
items.summary: The Central Bank of Ireland fined Coinbase Ireland €3,252,618 for safeguarding and outsourcing breaches covering the period from November 2020 through August 2025.

items.title: Solana leads weekly tokenized-equity DEX activity
items.summary: Solana reportedly reclaimed the top position in weekly decentralized-exchange spot volume for tokenized equities, highlighting renewed activity in blockchain-based securities markets.

items.title: European Central Bank plans tokenized-securities investment
items.summary: The European Central Bank plans to invest a small portion of reserves in euro-denominated tokenized securities, giving it direct exposure to blockchain-based financial markets.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic reports Claude Opus 5.5 advances in agentic coding
items.summary: Anthropic says Claude Opus 5.5 leads in agentic coding and knowledge-work tasks while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.

items.title: Moonshot AI launches Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Moonshot AI introduced Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3-trillion-parameter flagship model available through paid cloud services, with open weights planned for November 4.

items.title: NVIDIA releases compact Nemotron model for local agents
items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, an open small language model designed for local voice assistants, game characters, robots, and other edge applications.

items.title: Block unveils voice-only Dessa model
items.summary: Block announced Dessa, a research-preview full-duplex voice model trained from human speech without text or pretrained models. The company says it trained the system on a single NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 and plans early access for AI-safety researchers.

items.title: Google DeepMind reports embodied-reasoning gains with Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google DeepMind reported that Gemini 4 Argon achieved an 87% score on the ERQA embodied-reasoning benchmark and that synthesized training data improved a real robot’s tabletop-task success rate from 56% to 75%.

items.title: MiniMax launches M3.1 Flash
items.summary: MiniMax released M3.1 Flash, reporting API pricing of $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens, along with substantially higher speed than its predecessor.

items.title: Google publishes open-source ML Drift inference engine
items.summary: Google released ML Drift under the Apache 2.0 license as a cross-platform GPU compute engine for on-device artificial-intelligence and machine-learning inference.

items.title: Cadence introduces Maestro AI models for chip design
items.summary: Cadence Design Systems unveiled Maestro, a suite of customizable AI models for chip design that can run in private or public clouds and is backed by a collaboration with NVIDIA.

items.title: Researchers introduce RynnUnify embodied model
items.summary: Researchers at Alibaba’s DAMO Academy introduced RynnUnify, a 16-billion-parameter model combining embodied understanding, visual planning, and robot control, with reported gains over earlier systems on simulated and real-robot tasks.

items.title: OpenAI expands ChatGPT advertising availability
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly expanded ChatGPT Ads to 26 additional countries, bringing the service’s reported availability to 89 countries.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero releases on PS5 and PC
items.summary: Phantom Blade Zero is the headline release on Japan’s current gaming calendar, launching for PlayStation 5 and PC. Coverage also highlights strong early reviews for the action game.

items.title: Playable Archive revives canceled Paranormal Activity game prototype
items.summary: A reworked version of the canceled Paranormal Activity: Threshold prototype is now available for free under the name Playable Archive, with the original franchise references removed.

items.title: Xbox reportedly prepares additional layoffs
items.summary: Xbox is reportedly facing three more rounds of layoffs as the gaming division continues a major restructuring and business reset under CEO Asha Sharma.

items.title: Sonic x Shadow Generations surpasses three million sales
items.summary: SEGA says Sonic x Shadow Generations has sold more than three million copies worldwide.

items.title: Monster Hunter Wilds Switch 2 demo launches
items.summary: Capcom has released a prologue demo for Monster Hunter Wilds on Nintendo Switch 2, with preorders open ahead of the game’s December 4 launch.

items.title: No Man’s Sky coming to iOS on October 28
items.summary: No Man’s Sky is scheduled to launch on Apple’s iOS platform on October 28, expanding the space exploration game’s mobile availability.

items.title: 1win Team opens Esports World Cup 2026 with three Dota 2 wins
items.summary: 1win Team began its Esports World Cup 2026 campaign with three consecutive victories, according to gaming-esports coverage.
